questions.stem: The Gangasagar Mela, held at the confluence of the Ganga and the Bay of Bengal, attracts millions of pilgrims each year on which occasion?

options.option_text: Kartik Purnima — full moon in the month of Kartik (October–November)
Makar Sankranti — the sun's transit into Capricorn in mid-January
Maha Shivratri — the great night of Lord Shiva in February–March
Basant Panchami — the spring festival honoring Goddess Saraswati

questions.explanation: Gangasagar Mela is held on Makar Sankranti (around January 14–15) at Sagar Island, West Bengal, where pilgrims take a holy dip. The common confusion is Kartik Purnima, which is associated with Pushkar Fair, not Gangasagar.

questions.stem: The Tarnetar Mela of Gujarat is famous for tribal youth seeking life partners through a display of craft skill. Which distinctive hand-crafted item became the symbolic centrepiece of this tradition?

options.option_text: Embroidered kantha quilts displayed as signs of domestic skill
Bandhani tie-dye dupattas presented as tokens of betrothal
Intricately embroidered umbrellas (chhatri) showcasing needlework
Appliqué-work toran (door hangings) hung at the fair entrance

questions.explanation: At Tarnetar (Saurashtra, Gujarat), Rabari and other tribal women make richly embroidered umbrellas (chhatri) to display needlework skill; suitors judge prospective brides by the quality of their work. Kantha belongs to Bengal, Bandhani to Rajasthan — not linked to Tarnetar.

questions.stem: Ladakh's grandest monastery festival, Hemis, features masked Cham dances and is held to mark the birth anniversary of which religious figure?

options.option_text: Milarepa — the revered Tibetan yogi who attained enlightenment
Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche) — who brought Vajrayana Buddhism to Tibet
Tsongkhapa — founder of the Gelug (Yellow Hat) school of Tibetan Buddhism
Atisha Dipankara — the Bengali scholar who reformed Tibetan Buddhism

questions.explanation: Hemis Monastery belongs to the Drukpa Kagyu sect and celebrates the birthday of Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), who introduced Tantric Buddhism to Tibet. Tsongkhapa founded the Gelug school — the lineage of the Dalai Lama — which is a separate sect unrelated to Hemis.

questions.stem: The Wangala Festival, featuring the iconic 'Hundred Drums' ceremony, is the most important post-harvest celebration of which tribal community and in which state is it primarily observed?

options.option_text: Bodo tribe of Assam, honoring the Bathou deity Shiba at harvest
Mishing tribe of Assam, worshipping Ali the Sun God after reaping
Garo tribe of Meghalaya, honoring the fertility deity Saljong
Khasi tribe of Meghalaya, celebrating Ka Blei Nongthaw (Sun God)

questions.explanation: Wangala (Hundred Drums Festival) is the premier festival of the Garo people of Meghalaya, celebrated post-autumn harvest to honor Saljong, the Sun God of fertility. Bodo and Mishing are Assamese tribes with entirely different festivals (Bwisagu and Ali-Ai-Ligang respectively).

questions.stem: The town of Pushkar houses one of India's rarest temples, making its pilgrimage uniquely significant. Which deity of the Hindu Trinity — virtually without a major temple elsewhere in India — is enshrined there?

options.option_text: Lord Vishnu — the preserver deity worshipped at Badrinath shrine
Lord Brahma — the creator deity with no other major temple in India
Lord Shiva — worshipped at the 12 Jyotirlingas across India
Goddess Saraswati — Brahma's consort with a major shrine at Basara

questions.explanation: Pushkar's Jagatpita Brahma Mandir is considered the only major Brahma temple in India — unlike Vishnu (thousands of temples) and Shiva (12 Jyotirlingas). Option D is a deliberate trap: Saraswati does have a significant temple at Basara, Telangana, making Brahma's solitary temple even more distinctive.

questions.stem: The Ambubachi Mela at Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati draws thousands of Tantric devotees annually. The fair is triggered by the belief that the presiding goddess undergoes which natural phenomenon during the three-day closure?

options.option_text: Annual cosmic deep sleep (yoga nidra) signifying universal dissolution
Annual menstruation, symbolizing the earth goddess's creative fertility
Annual celestial marriage ceremony performed with Lord Shiva
Annual descent into the underworld followed by her resurrection

questions.explanation: Kamakhya (a premier Shakti Peetha) enshrines the yoni of Goddess Sati. The Ambubachi Mela marks the three-day menstruation of the earth goddess, during which the temple closes and the Brahmaputra is believed to run red. Yoga nidra (Option A) is associated with Lord Vishnu's Devshayani Ekadashi cycle, not Kamakhya.

questions.stem: The Chapchar Kut festival of Mizoram is unique among Northeast Indian festivals because it does NOT celebrate a harvest. Instead, it marks the completion of which specific phase of Jhum (shifting) cultivation?

options.option_text: Sowing of millet seeds after the onset of the first monsoon rains
First cutting of paddy — a thanksgiving to the Rice Goddess Khuangchawi
Clearing and burning of jungle undergrowth before the sowing season
Ploughing and terracing of hillside plots at the end of winter

questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut (February–March) is held after the strenuous work of felling and burning jungle for Jhum cultivation is done, but before sowing begins — making it a pre-sowing celebration, not a harvest festival. Option B (harvest thanksgiving) is the most seductive trap because most Indian tribal festivals are harvest-linked; Chapchar Kut is the rare exception tied to forest clearance.
